title: Your Significance and Purpose Within the Body of Christ
titleZh: 你在基督身體裡的重要性與目的
summaryZh: 聚集的目的，是各人帶著恩賜彼此建造、使人得力。
lines: It was believed that the reason we come together is for learning.
人們認為，我們聚在一起是為了學習。
And I don't want to diminish the value of the fact that we love to listen to and read the Scriptures, to study them together, and to learn the word of God.
我不想貶低這件事的價值：我們喜愛聆聽、閱讀聖經，一起研讀，也學習神的話語。
This is a significant part of our lives.
這是我們生命中很重要的一部分。
I would never want to diminish that in any way.
我絕不希望以任何方式貶低這件事。
But the problem is that this is not the standard that Jesus set.
但問題是，這不是耶穌所立下的準則。
Let me read to you what Jesus said.
讓我把耶穌說的話讀給你們聽。
He said in Luke chapter 17, I'll just read it to you.
祂在《路加福音》第十七章這樣說，我直接讀給你們聽。
He said, "Which of you, having a servant plowing or tending sheep, will say to him when he comes in from the field, 'Go quickly, sit down and eat.'"
祂說：「你們誰有僕人耕地或是放羊，從田裡回來，就對他說：『你快來坐下吃飯』呢？」
Would he not rather say to him, "Prepare my supper, and gird yourself and serve me while I eat and drink, and afterward you may eat and drink?"
「他豈不對他說：『你給我預備晚飯，束上帶子伺候我，等我吃喝完了，你才可以吃喝』嗎？」
Often the church meets together on Sunday.
We take out our spiritual knives and forks and say, "Jesus, feed us."
我們拿出屬靈的刀叉，說：「耶穌，餵養我們吧。」
And we are servants who have worked in the field all week.
我們就像整個星期都在田裡工作的僕人。
And sometimes we think that we really deserve the best seat at the meeting.
有時候，我們會覺得自己理當在聚會中坐最好的位子。
This is not a strict supervisor.
這不是一位嚴格的主管。
This is a loving father who does not seek worship.
這是一位慈愛的父親，祂不是在尋求敬拜。
祂在尋找的是仰慕祂的人。
The difference is that through his love he knows: I become like what I worship.
差別在於，祂深知，透過祂的愛，我會變得像我所敬拜的對象。
So he wants me to be a worshipper because then I become like him.
所以祂希望我成為敬拜者，因為這樣我就會變得像祂。
This is the best choice he can make for me.
這是祂能為我做出的最好選擇。
So he waits until I reach that state of tenderness where I truly serve him.
所以祂等候我，直到我進入那種柔軟的狀態，真正地服事祂。
So, our joint gathering has a very important purpose.
因此，我們一同聚集有非常重要的目的。
You can do it individually, in a small group, but there is something so profound and meaningful about gathering together here.
你可以個別做到，也可以在小組中做到；但在這裡一同聚集，有一種深刻而有意義的特質。
The expression, the sense of presence, what happens in these moments is simply extraordinary.
這種彰顯、同在的感受，以及此刻所發生的一切，實在非比尋常。
In addition, the Apostle Paul in 1 Corinthians 14 says: "When you come together, let each one have a psalm."
此外，使徒保羅在《哥林多前書》第十四章說：「你們聚會的時候，各人或有詩歌。」
Have a doctrine, a testimony, have something, bring something together.
或有教訓，或有見證；總之要有些東西，帶來一起分享。
So that when you come together as a people, you have something to contribute to others.
這樣，當你們作為一群人聚集時，就能帶些東西來貢獻給別人。
If you read 1 Corinthians 12, 13—the chapter on love, 14—chapters 12 and 14 are devoted to gifts.
你若讀《哥林多前書》第十二章、談愛的第十三章，以及第十四章，就會看到第十二章和第十四章都在談恩賜。
There is a dominant theme in the manifestation of the gifts of the Spirit, and that is the edification, exhortation, and strengthening of the body of Christ.
聖靈恩賜的彰顯有一個主要的主題，就是造就、勸勉並堅固基督的身體。
The Lord's purpose is for each of us to have a part in bringing strength to someone else.
主的心意是讓我們每個人都能參與其中，使別人得著力量。
So let me put it this way.

When we gather together, if you have not consciously and with effort worked to encourage, to strengthen, to help bring edification to the people in the meeting, then you have lost the reason why you are here.
我們聚集時，如果你沒有刻意並努力地鼓勵、堅固聚會中的人，幫助他們得著造就，那你就失去了來這裡的理由。
Yes, we are here to worship.
是的，我們來這裡是為了敬拜。
But the life of my human body works because each member contributes to the functioning of the other.
但我的身體之所以能運作，是因為每個肢體都對其他肢體的運作有所貢獻。
And when you interrupt that contribution, you create separation, and that separation is death.
當你打斷這種貢獻，就會造成分離，而分離就是死亡。
I'm not trying to instill guilt; I'm trying to set a goal.
我不是要讓你們心生罪咎，而是想要設定一個目標。
I'm trying to determine what you're good at.
我想要找出你擅長什麼。
You may or may not know it, but you may actually be that person who has the song.
你可能知道，也可能不知道，但你或許就是那個帶著詩歌的人。
This morning I jokingly told a story about Chris when he...
今天早上，我開玩笑地講了一個關於克里斯的故事，當時他……
I said we should have a song, and he started singing for Leslie at the first service.
我說我們應該來一首歌，於是他就在第一場聚會中唱歌給萊斯莉聽。
And I remembered how he came to visit my father, who was dying.
我想起他曾來探望我那時病危的父親。
And he said to my father, "I feel like I have to sing for you."
他對我父親說：「我覺得我得為你唱一首歌。」
And he asked, "Is there anything you want me to sing?"
他又問：「你想聽我唱什麼嗎？」
He says, "On a hill in the distance."
他說：「在遠方的一座山丘上。」
And Chris asked again, "Do you want me to sing the song 'On the Hill in the Distance'?"
克里斯又問：「你要我唱《在遠方的山丘上》這首歌嗎？」
He says, "No, I want you to sing on a hill from afar."
他說：「不，我要你在遠方的一座山丘上唱歌。」
